component: Component documentation path and CI naming

quotes.text:
# Note: doc_trees does not include the "comm/" prefix to paths
# Note: In order for CI to pick up the need to rebuild docs, documentation
#  paths must include a "docs/" directory.
doc_trees:
    adr: docs/adr
    addrbook: mail/components/addrbook/docs
    backend: mailnews/base/docs
    build: docs/build
    calendar: calendar/docs
    cxx: docs/cxx
    documentation: docs/docs
    exchange: mailnews/protocols/exchange/docs
    frontend: mail/base/docs
    inappnotifications: mail/components/inappnotifications/docs
    l10n: docs/l10n
    mots: docs/mots
    panorama: mailnews/db/panorama/docs
    rust: rust/docs
    storybook: mail/components/storybook/docs
    telemetry: docs/telemetry
    testing: docs/testing

source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The accepted docs/config.yml says tree paths omit comm/ and must include a docs directory for CI to notice changes. The source-docs task uses comm/**/docs/**. Add a component tree with the correct relative path and retain that directory convention; placing source documentation elsewhere without changing the task filter can miss rebuilds. Rust markdown filenames retain underscores in their existing family. This is a scoped documentation layout rule, not a global filename case rule.
title: Use a docs directory and the tree mapping for component documentation
